title: Risotto al tartufo
subtitle: Truffle risotto with truffle paste and Parmesan
excerpt: Risotto al tartufo is a butter-and-Parmesan risotto finished with truffle paste. Fresh truffle is the luxury version; truffle paste, widely available in Italian delis and supermarkets, delivers a clear truffle note without the cost. The base risotto must be immaculate: well-made rice is the vehicle, not the afterthought.
sourceNotes: Italian home-cooking tradition. Truffle risotto is popular across Umbria, Piedmont, and parts of Tuscany, where black and white truffles are found. The paste version is a practical alternative for home cooks. Methods drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian for truffle; in Italian cooking, tartufo nero (black truffle) is used cooked in sauces and pastas, while tartufo bianco (white truffle) from Alba is shaved raw over dishes at the last minute.

content.text: is a simple, clean risotto: butter, good stock, Parmesan, and truffle paste folded in at the end. The truffle goes in off the heat so the volatile flavour compounds don't cook off. A little goes a long way; start with a teaspoon and add more to taste.

items.prepNote: half for cooking, half cold for finish

content.text: Melt 40 g of butter in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat. Cook the shallots gently for 8 minutes. Add {{arborio-rice}} of rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the hot {{stock-vegetable}} of stock one ladle at a time over about 18 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is al dente. Season with salt.

Remove from the heat. Beat in the remaining 40 g of cold butter, the Parmesan, and {{truffle-paste}} of truffle paste. Taste; add more paste if you like a stronger truffle note. Rest, covered, for 2 minutes. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Paste added too early and the heat cooked off the volatile flavour compounds.
items.fix: Always add truffle paste off the heat, in the mantecatura step, never during cooking.

items.cause: Too little stock, or rested too long.
items.fix: Stir in a ladleful of hot stock just before serving. Risotto should flow slowly on the plate.

content.text: Truffle risotto comes from Umbria (black truffle country around Norcia and Spoleto) and Piedmont (white Alba truffle). In restaurants, fresh truffle is grated over the dish at the table. The paste version is the home-cook's answer: cheaper, available year-round, and still clearly truffle in flavour.
